best_for: Windows users who move large folders to NAS boxes and external drives and want proof every file arrived intact.
description:
TeraCopy is a file copy tool from Code Sector, which says it has sold it for 20 years and counts government agencies and universities among its users.

If a network share or drive drops out mid-copy, TeraCopy waits for it to come back. When the job ends, you can retry just the failed or skipped files. You can decide ahead of time how to handle name clashes, and run a PowerShell script when a copy finishes. The file list doubles as the log, with sizes and checksums for every file. You can pick which metadata to copy, such as timestamps or permissions, or copy only the folder structure.

points.title: A failed file does not stop the job
points.text: TeraCopy replaces Explorer's copy and move. If one file fails, it skips it and carries on, then shows you what was skipped. You come back to a finished job instead of a stalled dialog.

points.title: Checks the copy, not just the speed
points.text: It can verify copies with 17 checksum algorithms, and create or check checksum files. Locked files can be copied through Volume Shadow Copy.

points.title: Free is for home use
points.text: The free version covers verification, locked files and Explorer integration but is limited to 2 copy threads. Commercial use, multiple destinations, 3 or more threads and HTML or CSV reports need Pro or Business.

points.title: One payment, then major upgrades cost extra
points.text: The purchase page lists TeraCopy at $49.95, and a Pro license covers all of one person's own devices. Minor updates are free; existing owners get discounted pricing on future major versions. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Version 4 brings a new engine
points.text: TeraCopy 4 added a multi-threaded copy engine, a task queue, copying to several targets and receiving files over LocalSend.

points.title: Windows x64 only here
points.text: This listing covers a 64-bit Windows installer that installs for all users, and keeps 13 versions. Code Sector sells a separate Mac edition that is not listed here.
